question: The word 'Veda' is derived from which of the following root words? (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Vedi
Vid
Ved
Vit
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Vid

Explanation:
The word 'Veda' is derived from the Sanskrit root 'Vid', which means 'to know' or 'knowledge'. Thus, Veda literally means 'knowledge'. There are four Vedas: Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda, and Atharvaveda. Vedic literature includes Samhitas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas, and Upanishads. The Vedas are considered 'Shruti' (that which is heard) and are the oldest sacred texts of Hinduism. Other words like 'Vidya', 'Vidwan', 'Vedana' are also derived from the same root. Options like Vedi, Ved, and Vit are not related to the etymology of Veda.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ From which root is the word Veda derived? → Vid
☛ What does the root Vid mean? → To know
☛ Name the four Vedas. → Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda, Atharvaveda
☛ What are the Vedas called? → Shruti
☛ Another word derived from Vid root? → Vidya
question_hi: शब्द 'वेद' निम्नलिखित में से किस मूल शब्द से लिया गया है? (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: वेदी
विद्
वेद
वित्
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है विद्

Explanation:
शब्द 'वेद' संस्कृत धातु 'विद्' से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है 'जानना' या 'ज्ञान'। वेद शब्द का शाब्दिक अर्थ 'ज्ञान' होता है। चार वेदों में संहिताएँ, ब्राह्मण, आरण्यक और उपनिषद शामिल हैं। वैदिक साहित्य भारतीय संस्कृति और धर्म का सबसे प्राचीन ग्रंथ है। विद् धातु से ही 'विद्या', 'विद्वान', 'वेदना' जैसे शब्द भी बने हैं। वेदों को 'श्रुति' कहा जाता है, जो ईश्वर द्वारा प्रकट माने जाते हैं। अन्य विकल्प जैसे वेदी, वेद, वित्, वेद से संबंधित नहीं हैं।

☛ विद् धातु से बना एक अन्य शब्द? → विद्या

question: Which of the following sacred texts provide(s) most of the information about the social and economic life of the early Vedic period? (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Upnishadas
Mahabhatarta
Ramayana
Vedas
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Vedas

Explanation:
The early Vedic period (c. 1500-1000 BCE) socio-economic life is primarily reconstructed from the Vedas, especially the Rigveda. It describes social units like kula, grama, vish, and jana. The economy was based on pastoralism, agriculture, and barter trade, with cattle as the standard of wealth. Society was patriarchal, and yajnas were central. The Upanishads are philosophical texts of later period, while the Mahabharata and Ramayana are post-Vedic epics. Thus, the Vedas provide the most authentic information about early Vedic life.

Explanation:
प्रारंभिक वैदिक काल (लगभग 1500-1000 ई.पू.) के सामाजिक और आर्थिक जीवन की अधिकांश जानकारी वेदों से प्राप्त होती है। ऋग्वेद इस काल का सबसे प्राचीन ग्रंथ है, जिसमें राजनीतिक, सामाजिक और आर्थिक संरचना का विस्तृत वर्णन मिलता है। इसमें कुल, ग्राम, विश और जन जैसी सामाजिक इकाइयों का उल्लेख है। आर्थिक जीवन में कृषि, पशुपालन, व्यापार और वस्तु-विनिमय प्रमुख थे। गाय को धन का मापक माना जाता था। वैदिक समाज पितृसत्तात्मक था और यज्ञ सामाजिक जीवन का केंद्र था। अन्य विकल्प जैसे उपनिषद दार्शनिक ग्रंथ हैं, जबकि महाभारत और रामायण बाद के काल के हैं।

question:
Match the following.
Indus Valley Civilisaon Site Excavator(A). Harappa I. R Rao
(B). Dholavira II. JP Joshi
(C). Surkotada III. RS Bisht
(D). Lothal IV. Daya Ram Sahini (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: A-III; B-I; C-IV; D-II
A-II; B-IV; C-III; D-I
A-IV; B-III; C-II; D-I
A-I; B-III; C-II; D-IV
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is A-IV; B-III; C-II; D-I

Explanation:
Harappa was excavated in 1921 by Daya Ram Sahni, so (A)-(IV). Dholavira was excavated in the 1990s by R. S. Bisht, so (B)-(III). Surkotada was excavated in the 1970s by J. P. Joshi, so (C)-(II). Lothal was excavated in 1955-60 by S. R. Rao, so (D)-(I). All are major sites of the Indus Valley Civilization.

question: Which dynasty was overthrown by Chandragupta Maurya to establish the Mauryan Empire? (RRB JE CBT 2 (Electronics Engineering) ReExam (04/06/2025))
options: Gupta Dynasty
Kushan Dynasty
Shunga Dynasty
Nanda Dynasty
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Nanda Dynasty

Explanation:
Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the Nanda Dynasty by defeating its last ruler Dhanananda to establish the Mauryan Empire around 321 BCE. With the help of his mentor Chanakya (Kautilya), Chandragupta attacked Pataliputra and ended Nanda rule. The Nanda dynasty was founded by Mahapadma Nanda and was a powerful kingdom in Magadha. The Mauryan Empire became the first large empire in India, with its capital at Pataliputra.

☛ Founder of Nanda dynasty → Mahapadma Nanda
☛ Capital of Mauryan Empire → Pataliputra

question: The Shakas were defeated by which tribal group before entering India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: The Greeks
The Parthians
The Yueh-chis
The Huns
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Yueh-chis

Explanation:
The Shakas (Scythians) migrated to India from Central Asia. Before entering India, they were defeated by the Yueh-chis (also known as the Kushans). This conflict occurred around the 2nd century BCE. The Yueh-chis drove the Shakas from their original territories, forcing them to move southward into India, where they later established kingdoms in the western regions. The Shakas ruled areas like Ujjain and Mathura. The Yueh-chis themselves later entered India and founded the Kushan Empire, which controlled a large part of the Indian subcontinent. Thus, the Yueh-chis' defeat of the Shakas paved the way for the latter's entry into India.

☛ Which two major regions did the Shakas rule in India? → Ujjain and Mathura
☛ Which empire did the Yueh-chis establish in India? → Kushan Empire
☛ In which century did the Shakas enter India? → 1st century BCE
☛ What was the original homeland of the Yueh-chis and Shakas? → Central Asia
question_hi: भारत में प्रवेश करने से पहले शकों को किस आदिवासी समूह ने पराजित किया था? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 3)

पार्थियन
युह-चिस
हूण
solution_hi:

Explanation:
शक (सीथियन) मध्य एशिया से भारत की ओर आए। भारत में प्रवेश करने से पहले, उन्हें युह-चिस (जिन्हें कुषाण भी कहा जाता है) ने हराया था। यह संघर्ष लगभग दूसरी शताब्दी ईसा पूर्व में हुआ। युह-चिस ने शकों को उनके मूल क्षेत्र से खदेड़ दिया, जिसके बाद शक भारत की ओर बढ़े और यहां पश्चिमी क्षेत्रों में राज्य स्थापित किए। शकों ने उज्जैन और मथुरा जैसे क्षेत्रों पर शासन किया। युह-चिस स्वयं बाद में भारत आए और कुषाण साम्राज्य की स्थापना की, जिसने भारतीय उपमहाद्वीप के एक बड़े हिस्से पर शासन किया। इस प्रकार, युह-चिस ने शकों को पराजित कर उनके भारत आगमन का मार्ग प्रशस्त किया।

question: How many recognised styles of Vedic recitation (Pathas) are there? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (06/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Nine
Ten
Eleven
Seven
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Eleven

Explanation:
There are eleven recognised styles of Vedic recitation (Pathas). These different recitation methods were developed to preserve the original sound, accent, and order of the Vedic hymns. The major Pathas include Samhita, Pada, Krama, Jata, Mala, Shikha, Rekha, Dhwaja, Danda, Ratha, and Ghana. Among these, Ghana patha is considered the most complex. The aim of these recitation styles is to ensure the purity and accentual correctness of the Vedic mantras. They are of utmost importance in the Vedic tradition and are essential for preserving the oral tradition.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Which is the most complex Vedic patha? → Ghana patha
☛ What is the main purpose of Vedic pathas? → Preservation of original sound and accent
☛ In Pada patha, how are mantras divided? → Into individual words (padas)
☛ In Krama patha, what is the word pattern? → Each word is added progressively
question_hi: वैदिक पाठ की कितनी मान्यता प्राप्त अवस्थाएं हैं?  (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (06/06/2025) Shift 1)

ग्यारह

solution_hi:

Explanation:
वैदिक पाठ की ग्यारह मान्यता प्राप्त अवस्थाएं (पाठ) हैं। ये विभिन्न प्रकार के पाठ वेदों के मूल स्वर, उच्चारण और क्रम को संरक्षित करने के लिए विकसित किए गए थे। प्रमुख पाठों में संहिता, पदपाठ, क्रमपाठ, जटापाठ, मालापाठ, शिखापाठ, रेखापाठ, ध्वजपाठ, दण्डपाठ, रथपाठ और घनपाठ शामिल हैं। इनमें से घनपाठ सबसे जटिल माना जाता है। इन पाठों का उद्देश्य वैदिक मंत्रों की शुद्धता और स्वर सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित करना है। वैदिक परंपरा में इन पाठों का अत्यधिक महत्व है और ये मौखिक परंपरा को संरक्षित करने के लिए आवश्यक हैं।

question: Kanishka, the Kushana ruler, was a patron of which religion? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (06/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Buddhism
Christianity
Zoroastrianism
Jainism
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Buddhism

Explanation:
The Kushana ruler Kanishka (c. 78-144 CE) was a great patron of Buddhism, specifically of the Mahayana school. Under his patronage, the Fourth Buddhist Council was held at Kundalavana in Kashmir, presided over by Vasumitra with Ashvaghosha as vice-president. This council resulted in the translation of Buddhist texts into the Tibetan language. Kanishka's reign saw the flourishing of Gandhara and Mathura schools of art. He also built a large stupa at Purushapura (modern Peshawar).

☛ Capital of Kanishka → Purushapura (Peshawar)
☛ State religion of Kanishka → Buddhism
☛ Reign of Kanishka → 78 CE (start of Shaka era)
☛ Chairman of Fourth Buddhist Council → Vasumitra
☛ Court scholars of Kanishka → Ashvaghosha, Nagarjuna, Vasumitra

question: Who administered the agrahara lands during the post-Gupta period? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (06/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Monks
Feudal lords
Village assemblies
Brahmins
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Brahmins

Explanation:
During the post-Gupta period, the administration of agrahara lands was carried out by Brahmins. Agrahara lands were those donated by the king to Brahmins, often recorded on stone or copper plates. These Brahmins enjoyed tax-free rights and exercised administrative and judicial powers over these lands. This practice became more prominent after the Gupta period and contributed to the strengthening of the feudal system. Village assemblies and feudal lords were associated with the administration of other types of lands, while monks were generally not involved in land administration. Thus, agrahara lands were exclusively administered by Brahmins.

question: Whom did Chandragupta II marry after defeating the Saka king? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (06/06/2025) Shift 2)

question: An internal trade route during the post-Mauryan empires, Uttarapatha, connected the: (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (06/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: western and southern parts of India
southern and eastern parts of India
northern and southern parts of India with the northwestern region
northern and eastern parts of India with the northwestern region
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is northern and eastern parts of India with the northwestern region

Explanation:
During the post-Mauryan period, Uttarapatha was a major internal trade route. This route connected the northern and eastern parts of India (such as Pataliputra) with the northwestern region (such as Taxila). It ran parallel to the foothills of the Himalayas and facilitated trade, travel, and cultural exchange. Many towns and commercial centers were located along this route. In contrast, Dakshinapatha was a route associated with southern India. Thus, Uttarapatha specifically linked the north-east to the north-west.

question: Harappan seals were made mostly from which of the following? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Marble
Terracotta
Steatite
Iron
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Steatite

Explanation:
Harappan seals were mostly made from steatite, a soft stone that is easy to carve. Steatite is a type of talc mineral. The seals typically depict motifs like the unicorn, bull, elephant, tiger, and the Pashupati Shiva figure. They were used for trade and administrative purposes to stamp impressions. While some seals were also made from agate, chert, and faience, the majority are steatite. The seals bear inscriptions in the Harappan script, which remains undeciphered to date.

question: Which Mauryan ruler sent Buddhist missionaries to foreign countries? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 3)

question: Which animal/bird was commonly depicted on Harappan seals? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Horse
Peacock
Unicorn
Sparrow
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Unicorn

Explanation:
The most commonly depicted animal on Harappan seals was the Unicorn (a one-horned bull). These seals were typically made of steatite and often bore pictographic inscriptions. Besides the unicorn, other animals like elephant, tiger, rhinoceros, buffalo, and goat also appear, but the unicorn is the most frequent. Evidence of the horse in the Harappan civilization is very limited and disputed. Birds like peacock and sparrow are rarely depicted on seals. The unicorn is considered a religious or cultural symbol.

पट्टुप्पट्टु
सिलाप्पदिकाराम
एट्टुत्तोकाई
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है एट्टुत्तोकाई

Explanation:
प्राचीन तमिल साहित्य में आठ काव्य संकलनों का संग्रह 'एट्टुत्तोकाई' कहलाता है। इसका शाब्दिक अर्थ 'आठ संकलन' होता है। यह संगम साहित्य का एक महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा है, जो लगभग 300 ईसा पूर्व से 300 ईस्वी के बीच रचा गया था। एट्टुत्तोकाई में अकनानूरु, पुरनानूरु, ऐन्गुनूरु, पतित्रुपट्टु, परिपाडल, कलित्तोकै, कुरुंतोगै और नट्टिनाई जैसे संकलन शामिल हैं। ये रचनाएँ प्रेम, युद्ध, राजा और समाज के विभिन्न पहलुओं का वर्णन करती हैं। अन्य विकल्पों में तोलकाप्पियम व्याकरण ग्रंथ है, पट्टुप्पट्टु दस गीतों का संग्रह है, और सिलाप्पदिकारम एक महाकाव्य है।

question: Which material was used to make the famous 'Dancing Girl' statue that belonged to the Indus Valley Civilization? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Copper
Iron
Silver
Bronze
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bronze

Explanation:
The famous 'Dancing Girl' statue of the Indus Valley Civilization is made of bronze, an alloy of copper and tin. This figurine was discovered from Mohenjo-daro and dates back to around 2500 BCE. It is approximately 10.5 cm tall and is renowned for its artistic excellence and detailed design. The statue provides evidence of advanced metallurgy and sculpture in ancient India. Besides the 'Dancing Girl', other bronze items like animal figurines have also been found. The 'Dancing Girl' statue is one of the earliest known bronze sculptures in the world.

question: Chandragupta was succeeded by which of the following rulers, who ruled between 297 and 273 BCE? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Samprati
Ashoka
Devavarman
Bindusara
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bindusara

Explanation:
After Chandragupta Maurya, his son Bindusara ruled from 297 to 273 BCE. Bindusara was also known as 'Amitraghata' (slayer of enemies). He expanded the Mauryan Empire into southern India, conquering 16 kingdoms. During his reign, a rebellion occurred in Taxila, which was suppressed by his son Ashoka. The Greek ambassador Deimachus visited his court. Bindusara was a follower of the Ajivika sect. His rule strengthened the empire and consolidated the administrative system laid by his father.

☛ Which Greek ambassador visited Bindusara's court? → Deimachus
☛ Which sect did Bindusara follow? → Ajivika
☛ Who suppressed the Taxila rebellion during Bindusara's reign? → Ashoka
☛ How many kingdoms did Bindusara conquer in the south? → 16
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किस शासक ने चंद्रगुप्त का उत्तराधिकार प्राप्त किया, जिसने 297 और 273 ईसा पूर्व के बीच शासन किया? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 3)

देववर्मन

Explanation:
चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य के बाद उनके पुत्र बिन्दुसार ने 297 से 273 ईसा पूर्व तक शासन किया। बिन्दुसार को 'अमित्रघात' (शत्रुओं का संहारक) भी कहा जाता है। उन्होंने मौर्य साम्राज्य का विस्तार दक्षिण भारत तक किया, जहाँ उन्होंने 16 राज्यों पर विजय प्राप्त की। बिन्दुसार के शासनकाल में तक्षशिला में विद्रोह हुआ, जिसे उनके पुत्र अशोक ने दबाया। बिन्दुसार का दरबार में यूनानी राजदूत डाइमेकस आया था। वह आजीविक संप्रदाय के अनुयायी थे। उनके शासनकाल में साम्राज्य सुदृढ़ हुआ और प्रशासनिक व्यवस्था मजबूत हुई।

question: What was the name of Ramagupta's widow whom Chandragupta II marry after defeating the Saka king? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Dhruvadevi
Yasomati
Devatidevi
Kubernaga
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dhruvadevi

Explanation:
Chandragupta II, also known as Vikramaditya, married Dhruvadevi, the widow of his brother Ramagupta, after defeating the Saka king Rudrasimha III. Ramagupta was a weak ruler who offered Dhruvadevi to the Saka king after being defeated, but Chandragupta II opposed this, killed the Saka king, and rescued Dhruvadevi. This event is recorded in the history of the Gupta Empire. Dhruvadevi became Chandragupta II's wife, and their son Kumaragupta I later succeeded the throne. This marriage is considered significant in Gupta politics. The drama 'Devichandraguptam' by Vishakhadatta also mentions this story.

Explanation:

question: Who among the following issued the earliest land grant of the Maitraka family in 502 CE? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Guhasena
Dronasimha
Shiladitya
Dharapatta
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dronasimha

Explanation:
The Maitraka dynasty was founded in the 5th century and ruled over Saurashtra (Gujarat). In 502 CE, King Dronasimha issued the earliest known land grant of the Maitraka family. This grant is inscribed on a copper plate and belongs to the Vallabhi era. Dronasimha was one of the early Maitraka rulers who consolidated power after the decline of the Kshatrapas. His reign lasted approximately from 500 to 520 CE. The land grant was given to Brahmins, reflecting the royal patronage of religious institutions. Subsequent rulers like Guhasena, Shiladitya, and Dharapatta came later. Thus, the earliest grant is attributed to Dronasimha.

question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किसने 502 ईस्वी में मैत्रक परिवार की सबसे प्राचीन भूमि अनुदान जारी की थी? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: गुहासेन
द्रोणसिंह
शिलादित्य
धरापट्ट
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है द्रोणसिंह

Explanation:
मैत्रक वंश की स्थापना 5वीं शताब्दी में हुई थी, जिसने सौराष्ट्र (गुजरात) में शासन किया। 502 ईस्वी में राजा द्रोणसिंह ने सबसे प्राचीन भूमि अनुदान जारी किया था। यह अनुदान ताम्रपत्र पर उत्कीर्ण है और इसे वल्लभी युग से संबंधित माना जाता है। द्रोणसिंह मैत्रक शासकों में से एक थे, जिन्होंने क्षत्रपों के पतन के बाद अपनी स्थिति मजबूत की। उनका शासनकाल लगभग 500-520 ईस्वी तक रहा। यह भूमि अनुदान ब्राह्मणों को दिया गया था, जो उस काल में राज्य द्वारा धार्मिक संस्थाओं को समर्थन देने की प्रथा को दर्शाता है। मैत्रक वंश के शासक गुहासेन, शिलादित्य और धरापट्ट बाद में आए। अतः सबसे पुराना अनुदान द्रोणसिंह का है।

question: What was the officer responsible for looking after military stores during the reign of the Gupta Empire called? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Pilupati
Mahapratihara
Vishayapati
Ranabhandagarika
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ranabhandagarika

Explanation:
During the Gupta Empire, the military administration had designated officers for various duties. The Ranabhandagarika was the officer responsible for looking after military stores, including weapons, rations, and other essential supplies. This role was crucial for maintaining combat readiness. Other options: Pilupati was the officer in charge of elephants, Mahapratihara was the chief gatekeeper or palace guard, and Vishayapati was the provincial governor. The term 'Ranabhandagarika' is derived from 'rana' (war) and 'bhandagara' (storehouse). This position highlights the organized nature of Gupta military logistics.

question_hi: गुप्त साम्राज्य के शासनकाल में सैन्य भंडार की देखभाल के लिए उत्तरदायी अधिकारी को क्या कहा जाता था? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 1)

महाप्रतिहार
विषयपति
रणभंडागारिक

Explanation:
गुप्त साम्राज्य में सैन्य प्रशासन की एक महत्वपूर्ण इकाई थी। रणभंडागारिक वह अधिकारी था जो सैन्य भंडारों की देखभाल करता था, जिसमें हथियार, राशन और अन्य सैन्य सामग्री शामिल थी। यह पद गुप्त साम्राज्य की केंद्रीय सैन्य व्यवस्था का हिस्सा था। अन्य विकल्प: पिलुपति हाथियों का अधिकारी था, महाप्रतिहार द्वारपाल या मुख्य रक्षक था, और विषयपति प्रांतीय प्रशासक था। रणभंडागारिक शब्द 'रण' (युद्ध) और 'भंडागार' (भंडार) से मिलकर बना है। यह पद साम्राज्य की युद्ध-तैयारी में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता था।
